parsed.explanation: Exposure is dominated by state actors: routine pretextual police detention and on-the-spot extortion against trans people, remand beyond constitutional limits, and in custody nonconsensual medical procedures plus court-ordered 'gender determination' (High Court, Aug 2025), with no implementing statute enacted. Sodomy sections 162/165 (14-21 years) remain good law pending an unresolved appeal; no SOGI anti-discrimination statute exists and border treatment of trans travellers is not documented. Mitigation is real but partial: courts have repeatedly ruled for trans people (2018, 2023, 2025, 2026) and an LGBTQ killer drew 50 years, yet police practice continues unremedied. No execution is in force; the Family Protection Bill is not law.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No source covers entry, visa or border screening of trans travellers, so entry friction can be neither credited nor charged; visitor documents are home-issued and no rejection of foreign markers is recorded.
entry_documents.interaction: Document checks arise mainly through police street stops rather than the border; a mismatch encountered there could escalate an extortion stop into an investigation, but this chain is inferential, not documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: routine pretextual police detention ('drunk and disorderly'), on-the-spot extortion of 5,000 shillings, remand beyond the constitutional period without charges; in custody, nonconsensual medical procedures and court-ordered 'gender determination' found by the High Court in Aug 2025; cell placement by sex unresolved.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Aug 2025 High Court found torture, equality, dignity and privacy violations and directed a Transgender Protection Rights Act; no enacted legislation recorded. Compensation awarded in the 2015 forced-examination matter in 2024.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A street stop can escalate to detention, where documented custody practices (birth-sex placement uncertainty, invasive examinations) apply; foreign nationality offers no documented exemption.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Documented: trans people fear using sex-designated bathrooms in entertainment areas for fear of being accused of sexual crimes (NHRC 2012); police reported as uncertain whether to place trans detainees in male or female cells.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Not documented. The 2025 prison-rights judgment addresses dignity in custody but no facility-access rule for visitors is recorded.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility fear compounds police-stop exposure: using a bathroom can trigger the accusation that then invites police contact and extortion.

care_services.exposure: Documented: a trans patient completed all required processes yet was denied surgery at a national referral hospital without reasons, appeal unsuccessful (2012); no framework for gender-affirming care; visitor entitlement to care not addressed.
care_services.protection: Government affirmed non-discrimination in access to services including HIV prevention (2012 UN submission); courts have ordered rights protections, though unimplemented.
care_services.interaction: A medical emergency could out a traveller to staff; no documented refusal-of-emergency-care case and no documented visitor entitlement.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented: police harassment and extortion as routine (26 interviews, two cities; NHRC 2011; NGO 2020-21); sections 162/165 upheld in 2019 with appeal unresolved; no SOGI anti-discrimination statute; stalled Family Protection Bill (not law) proposes death for aggravated homosexuality.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Courts: 2018 forced anal examinations unconstitutional; 2023 Supreme Court association ruling; Aug 2025 trans-prison rights judgment; May 2026 gender-marker ruling; intersex recognised as third gender.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing operates through police discretion rather than a trans-specific statute; the sodomy sections supply a legal pretext if a visitor is read as same-sex conduct.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. The Children Act's adoption ineligibility is resident-facing; no source addresses a trans visitor travelling with a minor, school or custody interactions, or family-visiting risks for children.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented: widespread anti-LGBTQ+ sentiment, violence claims dismissed by a 2019 High Court for purported lack of evidence, public-crowd exposure when a partner discovers sex status, one documented killing of an activist (Dec 2024). No trans-specific or general homicide rates, so magnitude cannot be stated.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 50-year sentence for that killing; national human-rights commission's Sept 2025 comprehensive documentation with 14+ organisations; active LGBTIQ+ civil society within a restrictive civic space.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Weak investigative follow-through on violence claims is documented historically, but the 2024 sentence shows courts do punish killers.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Court directives unimplemented (no Transgender Protection Rights Act recorded); police extortion unremedied; status of sections 162/165 appeal, the Family Protection Bill, and border treatment all unresolved in this inventory.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts demonstrably grant relief: compensation (2024), association (2023), prison-rights judgment (2025), gender-marker ruling (2026), with a government accepted non-discrimination interpretation.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists at judgment stage but implementation sits with an unresponsive parliament, so street-level exposure persists despite paper victories.

anchor_checks.comparison: Meridia documents transport-police extortion, document confiscation and overnight cells with a dismissive oversight board and no execution. This dossier matches that police-extortion pattern and adds an upheld 14-21 year sodomy statute plus documented custody abuse (nonconsensual procedures), but offsets with stronger, repeated court victories for trans people and a 50-year murder sentence. Net slightly above 0.25-B.

Karthovia has an unwritten instruction to stop trans visitors, hours of questioning, occasional fines, and courts that formally accept complaints but defer to police. Comparable tier: here detention is documented as routine with extortion, but the custody branch is worse (state-performed medical procedures) while courts have actually delivered trans-rights rulings rather than deferring. Similar level.

Valdoria's friction is registration and checkpoint delay with possible overnight holding, remedies partially effective, no execution. This dossier is materially worse: state-perpetrated extortion as routine practice, documented custody abuse, an enforced sodomy statute on the books, and no gender-recognition pathway, so it sits well below 0.55-A despite stronger judiciary.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is a court-advancing but unimplementing state: successive judgments ban forced examinations, protect association, order prison dignity and gender-marker change, yet parliament enacts nothing and police practice — pretextual detention, extortion, remand abuse — continues as the traveller's most likely adverse encounter. The sodomy sections remain good law pending appeal, giving officials a latent pretext, while no SOGI anti-discrimination statute or border-screening record exists (entry exposure is an open question, not a known good). For an outed visitor the realistic severity ladder runs from extortion/humiliation (2-3) up to custody abuse if arrested (4); no execution is in force. Recourse via courts is documented but too slow to deter street-level exposure, and the pending Family Protection Bill marks a hostile trajectory.
